title: Objective interpretation of assent
summary: Objective interpretation of assent asks what a party’s words and conduct reasonably communicated in their actual context, including relevant knowledge shared by the parties.
notes:
Lucy enforced a signed land-sale agreement where the purchaser genuinely and reasonably understood it as serious, despite the seller’s claimed private joke. Specht declined to infer agreement to terms whose existence was not reasonably brought to the user’s attention. These decisions show why context and notice matter. Objective interpretation does not require ignoring everything either party actually knew: shared knowledge of a joke or another meaning can change what the communication reasonably conveys.

Lucy protects a genuine and reasonable understanding despite a private joke. Keller involves shared knowledge of a joke, and Leonard concerns the reasonable meaning of an advertisement. Specht asks what a download communicates when notice is hidden. The opposing scholarly passages ask how far an objective account should exclude evidence of actual intention. A slogan that subjective intention never matters would erase important distinctions in this reading.
